label: Dify (OpenAI-API-compatible model provider plugin)
version: langgenius/dify-official-plugins main@60804e30f6fa41fbe890c02c9849b0bdbe28d13a (models/openai_api_compatible, plugin manifest version 0.0.83) + dify_plugin SDK v0.10.2 (langgenius/dify-plugin-sdks@3345471536c6a438884ac4942a2425b6627567f9, pinned in the plugin's uv.lock) + langgenius/dify 1.19.0 (8e689e868b63b6dd2b449d0eb568ca5cc7127759) for conversation-name generation

sources.note: _generate(): the actual chat request. Headers Content-Type + Accept-Charset: utf-8 (+ extra_headers) + Authorization Bearer if api_key; URL = endpoint_url.rstrip('/') + '/chat/completions'; body = {model: endpoint_model_name or model, stream, **model_parameters, messages, [tools/tool_choice | functions], [stop], [user]}; posted with python-requests, status != 200 -> InvokeError.
_join_endpoint_url: urljoin(endpoint_url.rstrip('/') + '/', 'chat/completions'). The plugin does NOT append /v1: the user must type the /v1 themselves.

Stream parser: lines split on the credential 'stream_mode_delimiter' (default '\n\n'); ':' comment events skipped; 'data:' prefix stripped; '[DONE]' skipped; non-JSON event ends the stream with finish_reason 'Non-JSON encountered.'; chunk with 'error' and no 'choices' raises; usage taken from any chunk; chunk_json['choices'] is indexed directly (KeyError if the key is missing); empty choices skipped; finish_reason = last non-empty choice's finish_reason.
Non-stream parser: choices[0]; message['content'] indexed directly (KeyError if absent); usage optional but if present needs prompt_tokens AND completion_tokens; id/model optional.

Message conversion: user str -> {role,content:str}; user list -> parts text/image_url(+detail)/video_url; assistant -> {role,content} (+tool_calls when function_calling_type == tool_call); system -> {role:'system'}; tool -> {role:'tool',content,tool_call_id}; 'name' added when set (not for tool). Dify never emits the 'developer' role.

Credential validation request: POST chat/completions {model, max_tokens: validate_credentials_max_tokens or 5, messages:[{role:user,content:'ping'}]} (no 'stream' key) or, with stream_mode_auth='use', max_tokens 10 + stream:true.
_validate_credentials_response: status must be 200; for non-stream the body must be JSON whose 'object' is 'chat.completion' (empty/missing 'object' is tolerated and filled in).

Plugin _invoke(): adds stream_options {include_usage:true} when stream and credential stream_include_usage != disabled (L773-L783); forwards reasoning_effort when set (L704-L717); maps max_tokens -> max_completion_tokens for endpoint model names matching ^(?:[\w-]+\.)*(o1|o3|gpt-5|gpt-6) when token_param_name=auto (L750-L765, L52-L54); drops 'user' when user_identity_support=no_support (L767-L771); structured output legacy path (L638-L660); non-standard thinking keys only in 'extended' compatibility mode (L677-L698).
validate_credentials(): for names matching o1/o3/gpt-5/gpt-6 validates through the openai python SDK (max_completion_tokens 16); otherwise falls back to the SDK base validation above.

UI fields: 'Model Name' (placeholder 'Enter full model name'), 'API Key', 'API Base URL' (placeholder 'Base URL, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1'), 'model name for API endpoint', 'Completion mode' (default chat), 'Model context size' (default 4096). Defaults further down: Function Call Type=no_call (L470-L479), Vision=no_support, Include Usage in Stream=enabled (L434-L443), User Identity Support=support (L406-L415), stream_mode_delimiter '\n\n' (L650-L657), api_type=chat_completions (L358-L367), compatibility_mode=strict (L336-L345).

Customizable model schema: sampling parameter rules exposed in the UI = temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens (default 512, max = 'Upper bound for max tokens', default 4096). Only parameters the app/workflow actually has enabled are forwarded.

Auto conversation name: invoke_llm(prompt_messages=[UserPromptMessage(CONVERSATION_TITLE_PROMPT + query)], model_parameters={'max_tokens': 500, 'temperature': 1}, stream=False); answer parsed as JSON with key 'Your Output' (json_repair fallback), empty -> falls back to the query.
invoke_llm passes data.user_id (from the Dify core dispatch payload) as the 'user' argument of _invoke, which becomes the top-level 'user' request field when truthy.

setup.baseUrl: http://host.docker.internal:8787/v1  (WITH /v1; the plugin only appends '/chat/completions'). Dify > Settings > Model Provider > install 'OpenAI-API-compatible' > Add Model > field 'API Base URL'. A Dify self-hosted stack runs plugin code inside the plugin_daemon container, so 'localhost' means that container: use host.docker.internal (or the host LAN IP) and make sure the gateway listens on it.
setup.model: 'Model Name' = agent name exactly as the gateway expects (e.g. agent/sample). Optional 'model name for API endpoint' overrides the name sent on the wire. Model Type LLM, 'Completion mode' = Chat. Dify never calls GET /v1/models: models are added by hand.
setup.apiKey: 'API Key' (optional field; if empty NO Authorization header is sent). Sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'.
setup.notes:
Request transport is python-requests, server-side (no CORS). Adding a model runs a credential check (POST chat/completions 'ping', max_tokens 5) and the model is rejected if it is not HTTP 200 with a JSON body whose object is 'chat.completion' (or empty). Streaming parse is very literal: events MUST be separated by a blank line made of '

' (a CRLF-only 'data: ...

' stream is not split by the default delimiter and fails with 'Non-JSON encountered'), each event must be a single 'data: {...}' line (an 'event:' line before it breaks JSON parsing), and every JSON chunk must contain a 'choices' key (usage-only chunks must send choices: []). Dify's default 'Function Call Type' is 'Not Support' so tools are NOT sent unless the operator selects 'Tool Call'. Defaults to non-vision: image parts are only sent if 'Vision Support' is enabled. Which sampling parameters appear in the body depends on the app's/workflow node's model parameter toggles (UI defaults not verified).

cases.title: Add-model credential validation: tiny non-stream 'ping' with max_tokens 5

evidence.note: Exact data dict: {'model': endpoint_model_name or model, 'max_tokens': validate_credentials_max_tokens or 5, 'messages': [{'role':'user','content':'ping'}]}. Headers: Content-Type + Authorization only (no Accept-Charset here); python-requests adds User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Encoding, Connection.

cases.notes: Must be HTTP 200 and JSON. If 'object' is present it MUST equal 'chat.completion', otherwise validation fails; a missing/empty 'object' is tolerated. Nothing else in the body is checked. If this fails with 'budget_tokens'/'thinking' in the error text the plugin retries once with an extra 'thinking': {'type':'disabled'} key (only on that error path). If max_tokens is rejected with 'Invalid max_output_tokens'/'integer_below_min_value' it retries through the openai SDK with max_tokens 16.

cases.title: Credential validation with 'stream_mode_auth = use': streaming ping, max_tokens 10

evidence.note: Only when the credential stream_mode_auth is 'use' (default 'not_use'): data['max_tokens'] = validate_credentials_max_tokens or 10, data['stream'] = True; response is not parsed beyond HTTP 200.

cases.notes: In stream-validation mode only the status code is checked; no stream_options key is sent here.

cases.title: Normal streaming chat: system + user messages, stream_options.include_usage (default)

evidence.note: stream_options {'include_usage': True} is injected whenever stream is true and the credential 'Include Usage in Stream' is not Disabled (default enabled). Body order = model, stream, model_parameters (here only stream_options), messages. No 'user', tools, max_tokens unless configured.

cases.notes: Parser details: (1) events split on '\n\n'; (2) each event must be exactly 'data: <json>' (after stripping 'data:'); '[DONE]' is skipped, not required; (3) EVERY JSON chunk is read via chunk_json['choices'] -> a chunk without a 'choices' key raises KeyError (the final usage chunk must carry choices: []); (4) usage is taken from whichever chunk has a truthy 'usage' (falls back to a local token estimate over messages[0] only if absent); (5) finish_reason is whatever the LAST chunk that has a non-empty choices[] carried (a late chunk with finish_reason null would overwrite it); (6) delta.role / chunk id / object are never read; (7) a non-JSON event silently terminates the stream. The Content-Type of the response is NOT checked. Content is read from delta.content, plus delta.reasoning_content / delta.reasoning which Dify wraps into <think>...</think>.

cases.title: Streaming chat including the top-level 'user' field (User Identity Support = Support, default)

evidence.note: The code adds data['user'] = user whenever 'user' is truthy and the plugin keeps it unless user_identity_support == 'no_support' (L767-L771). The value is data.user_id from the Dify dispatch payload (plugin_executor.py L308-L324); that it is a Dify account/end-user UUID and present for app runs is inferred (api/core/plugin/impl/model_runtime.py binds user_id=self.user_id).

cases.notes: 'user' is a UUID-like string in Dify. Some gateways reject unknown optional fields; Dify has a per-model switch for exactly that reason.

cases.title: Streaming chat with every UI sampling parameter enabled + stop (settings maxed out)

evidence.note: Parameter rule names: temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens (these are the only sampling keys the plugin declares). They are spread into the body right after 'stream' (L555-L559); 'stop' is appended after messages (L598-L599). Values are examples within the declared ranges.

cases.notes: No top_k, seed, n, logit_bias, response_format (unless structured output is on), tool keys here. Dify has no per-model 'n' or 'seed'.

cases.title: Automatic conversation name: non-stream, single user message, max_tokens 500 / temperature 1

evidence.note: model_parameters={'max_tokens': 500, 'temperature': 1}, stream=False, prompt_messages=[UserPromptMessage(content=CONVERSATION_TITLE_PROMPT + query)]. It is run with the app's model (or the tenant default LLM when none is resolved). The prompt text itself is a long instruction defined in core.llm_generator.prompts (not reproduced here).

messages.content:
<CONVERSATION_TITLE_PROMPT: instructions to answer with a JSON object {"Your Output": "<short title>"}>
Tell me a joke

cases.notes: Non-stream parser: choices[0] must exist; choices[0].message.content is indexed directly (KeyError if missing; content null would break the later title step); 'usage' is optional but when present MUST contain numeric prompt_tokens and completion_tokens; 'id' and 'model' optional. The title step then JSON-parses the content for key 'Your Output' (json_repair tolerant) and falls back to the user's query text when the content is empty. 'stream_options' is NOT sent for non-stream calls.

cases.title: User message whose content is an array containing only text parts

evidence.note: The conversion code turns any list content into [{'type':'text','text':...}, ...]. Whether Dify's workflow LLM node produces a text-only list (e.g. text + an empty/filtered file variable) rather than a plain string is inferred; plain-text chats use a string.

cases.notes: The gateway should accept content as either a string or an array of {type:'text'} parts.

cases.title: Vision-enabled model with an image file: text part + image_url part with detail

evidence.note: Shape verified: {'type':'image_url','image_url':{'url': data, 'detail': 'high'|'low'}}. 'data' is a base64 data URI by default or a signed remote URL depending on Dify's file-sending setting (multimodal send format) - inferred. Only sent when the model has 'Vision Support' enabled (default off). Audio parts are also encoded as image_url with a data URI; video as video_url; documents as {'type':'file','file':{'file_data','filename'}} when those supports are enabled.

cases.notes: Image input (docs/images.md): the data-URL image is decoded, checked and stored as an input file of the caller, and reaches an image-capable agent (the lab fixture agent declares image input) in its provider's own image shape. A text-only agent answers 400 unsupported_content with error.param on this part instead.

cases.title: Function Call Type = Tool Call: tools array + tool_choice 'auto' (no parallel_tool_calls)

evidence.note: tool_call mode: data['tool_choice'] = 'auto'; data['tools'] = [PromptMessageFunction(function=tool).model_dump()] = {'type':'function','function':{name, description, parameters}}. In 'function_call' mode the legacy 'functions' array is sent instead (no tool_choice). Default mode is 'Not Support' (nothing sent). Tool objects below are an example.

messages.content: What is the weather in Paris?

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the current weather for a city

cases.notes: Tool-call deltas are merged by tool_call id: a delta with a function name but no id gets a generated id; a delta with no id appends to the LAST tool call; arguments are concatenated; the result is emitted as one final chunk. Tool calls in the non-stream parser are read from message.tool_calls only in tool_call mode.

cases.title: Agent round 2: assistant message with tool_calls (content empty) followed by a role:tool message

evidence.note: Conversion verified: assistant -> {'role':'assistant','content': message.content, 'tool_calls':[tool_call.dict()]} with tool_call.dict() = {id, type:'function', function:{name, arguments}}; tool -> {'role':'tool','content', 'tool_call_id'}. The assistant content is whatever Dify stored for that turn: '' is the common value but null is possible (AssistantPromptMessage.content is optional) - inferred.

messages.content: What is the weather in Paris?

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the current weather for a city

cases.notes: Gateway should tolerate assistant content '' or null together with tool_calls, and tool messages without a 'name'.

cases.title: Thinking Mode Support enabled + Reasoning effort set: standard reasoning_effort key forwarded

evidence.note: reasoning_effort (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh) is only offered when 'Thinking Mode Support' is 'supported' or 'only_thinking_supported' (rules at L328-L358); it is forwarded as a top-level body key regardless of the strict/extended compatibility mode. In 'extended' mode ADDITIONAL non-standard keys (chat_template_kwargs, thinking, enable_thinking, reasoning_format) are sent - not in this case.

cases.notes: Off by default. Reasoning text coming back in delta.reasoning_content or delta.reasoning is rendered inside <think> tags; when thinking is configured 'not supported' Dify filters <think> blocks out of the reply.

cases.title: Structured output = 'supported' (legacy): response_format json_object + schema injected into the system prompt

evidence.note:
With structured_output_support='supported' and response_format=json_schema the plugin prepends 'Your response must be a JSON object that validates against the following JSON schema, and nothing else.
JSON Schema: ```json
<schema>
```' to the (first) system message and sends response_format {'type':'json_object'}. With structured_output_support='native' it instead sends response_format {'type':'json_schema','json_schema': <parsed schema object>} (SDK L526-L551; exact schema envelope not verified). Default is not_supported (no response_format).

messages.content:
Your response must be a JSON object that validates against the following JSON schema, and nothing else.
JSON Schema: ```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"answer":{"type":"string"}},"required":["answer"]}
```

You are a helpful assistant.

cases.title: Endpoint model name matching o1/o3/gpt-5/gpt-6 (token_param_name=auto): max_tokens becomes max_completion_tokens

evidence.note: Regex ^(?:[\w-]+\.)*(o1|o3|gpt-5|gpt-6) (IGNORECASE, anchored at start, optional 'prefix.' segments) is tested on endpoint_model_name or the Dify model name; credential 'Token parameter name' = max_completion_tokens forces it for any name, = max_tokens disables it.

cases.notes: Included so the gateway proves it accepts max_completion_tokens. An agent literally named like 'o3-helper' or 'gpt-5-bot' triggers this shape automatically; the model-name validation path for these names uses the openai python SDK instead (headers then include OpenAI/Python User-Agent and X-Stainless-*).
